神经科学 / 神经病学 / 精神病学 / 神经外科史上的今天。

神经信息学

学术发现1990神经科学经典里程碑

二十世纪最后十年，生命科学领域正经历一场静默而深刻的革命。传统生物学研究依赖实验观察与手工记录，但神经科学却面临一个前所未有的困境：脑研究所产生的数据量呈指数级增长，从单个神经元的电生理记录到大规模脑成像图谱，从分子水平的受体分布到行为学的追踪数据，这些信息分散在不同实验室、不同格式、不同国家的论文与硬盘中，彼此割裂，难以整合。研究者常常花费数月时间重复他人已完成的实验，或因为无法检索到关键数据集而错过重要发现。这种“数据孤岛”现象严重制约了脑科学的整体推进，而彼时计算机科学与互联网技术刚刚开始成熟，为信息的存储、检索与共享提供了技术可能。正是在这一背景下，神经信息学作为一门新兴交叉学科应运而生。

1990年代，神经信息学正式被提出并逐步确立其学科框架。其核心思想并不复杂：将神经科学领域海量的实验数据、影像资料、基因表达谱、电生理记录以及相关文献，通过统一的数据库标准和计算工具进行系统化整合，使研究者能够像查询图书馆目录一样便捷地访问全球脑研究资源。这一理念的提出，标志着神经科学从“个体作坊式”研究向“大规模协作式”科学范式的转变。其具体机制包括建立标准化的数据格式与元数据规范，开发能够自动解析和标注神经数据的软件工具，以及构建分布式网络平台，让不同地区的实验室能够实时上传、共享和交叉验证数据。更重要的是，神经信息学强调计算模型与实验数据的结合——通过算法对海量数据进行模式识别、统计分析和模拟仿真，从而揭示单个实验难以发现的规律，例如神经元群体编码的时空动态、脑区之间的连接权重变化等。这一学科并非单纯的技术堆砌，而是试图建立一套“脑数据的通用语言”，让不同层次、不同模态的神经信息能够在同一框架下互操作。

神经信息学的影响迅速超出了实验室范畴。它直接催生了后来一系列大型脑数据库与共享平台的建设，使得人类基因组计划之后，脑科学也拥有了自己的“数据基础设施”。在后续的二十余年中，这一领域的发展为神经退行性疾病研究提供了大规模对照数据，为精神疾病的生物标志物筛选提供了计算工具，也为脑机接口和人工智能算法提供了训练素材。更深远的影响在于方法论层面：神经信息学确立了“数据驱动发现”的研究模式，研究者不再仅仅依赖假设-验证的线性路径，而是可以通过对海量数据的挖掘提出新问题、新假说。这种范式转变与同期兴起的“大数据”思潮相互呼应，使神经科学成为生命科学中最具计算特色的分支之一。

对今天的启示而言，神经信息学的诞生提醒我们，科学进步往往并非源于某个孤立的重大发现，而是来自对研究基础设施的重新思考。当数据成为科学的核心资产，如何组织、共享、验证和复用数据，就与设计实验本身同等重要。当前人工智能热潮中，神经科学数据与深度学习模型的结合，正是神经信息学理念的延续与深化。同时，它也带来一个持续存在的挑战：数据标准化与隐私保护之间的平衡，以及如何确保共享数据的质量与伦理合规。回望1990年代那个学科初创的时刻，我们看到的不仅是一个技术工具的集合，更是一种科学精神的转型——即承认脑的复杂性远超个体认知，唯有通过集体智慧的整合，才能逼近其奥秘。神经信息学的故事，至今仍在塑造着每一位神经科学家的工作方式，也提醒着后来者：真正的突破，有时就藏在那些看似枯燥的数据组织与计算工具之中。

Deep Brain Stimulation Using Animal Models of Parkinson's Disease.

Paper Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.) pubmed 2027 doi:10.1007/978-1-0716-5699-0_26 Deep brain stimulationBrain stimulation
命中依据
  • TI="deep brain stimulation"

The use of deep brain stimulation (DBS) as a therapy for neurological disorders, especially Parkinson's disease (PD), is widely applied in the field of functional neurosurgery. Both the subthalamic nucleus and the globus pallidus interna are major targets for PD. Experimental DBS is performed using animal models to evaluate new indications and promote advancements in technology. In this article, we reviewed our experience with the concept of experimental DBS, including its development and validation. The following work aims to establish that experimental DBS in animals is an adequate tool for exploring new indications for DBS and to further refine DBS technology.

Understanding Posttraumatic Growth Following Lifetime Trauma: Longitudinal Latent Class Analysis Including Cognitive Processes.

Paper Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress pubmed 2026-12 doi:10.1002/smi.70241
命中依据
  • AB=depression
  • AB=PTSD

The nature of posttraumatic growth (PTG), defined as positive changes that can occur after a traumatic event (TE), is debated due to its complex and dynamic relationship with psychological adjustment. Although heterogeneous PTG trajectories have been identified, the processes underlying their development over time remain insufficiently understood. This study, adopting a person-centred approach, seeks to identify latent classes with distinct multivariate trajectories (PTG, PTSD, positive thinking, deliberate rumination) over 1 year and their sociodemographic, event-related, and psychosocial determinants. A sample of 244 adults exposed to a TE completed, at three points spaced 6 months apart, online questionnaires assessing PTG and psychosocial variables. Sociodemographic and event-related characteristics were collected at baseline. Latent classes with distinct multivariate trajectories were identified. Analyses of variance, chi-square tests, and multinomial logistic regression tested differences between classes and their predictors. Stress Related to Individual Life Circumstances and Worry About Global Issues as Distinct but Related Predictors of Psychological Health in Canadian Young Adults.

Paper Stress and health : journal of the International Society for the Investigation of Stress pubmed 2026-12 doi:10.1002/smi.70242
命中依据
  • AB=depression

Young adults' psychological health has deteriorated in many developed countries over the past decade, including Canada. To further understand this negative trend, this study documented stress related to individual life circumstances (e.g., finances, housing) and worry about global issues (e.g., climate change, world conflicts) and investigated their cross-sectional and prospective associations with psychological health. A sample of 1149 individuals from Canada (Mage = 24.84, SDage = 2.75) completed an online questionnaire in Winter 2025. Of these, 517 participants completed a six-month follow-up. Between 25% and 64% of participants reported being moderately to highly stressed about their life circumstances. Similarly, 32%-43% reported being frequently to constantly worried about global issues. Individual stressors were associated with greater distress (anxiety, depression) and lower well-being at T1, but not at T2, whereas global-issue-related worry was associated with greater distress at T1, and with higher anxiety and lower well-being at T2. OBJECTIVES: Efforts to examine the influence of genetics in the efficacy of lithium using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several loci. Here, we report new cases and meta-analyses to combine previous efforts. METHODS: We report data from 1259 participants with bipolar disorder (BD) recruited at University College London who had been treated with lithium. The data come from three waves of genotyping on different arrays. The GWAS data from each array was analysed separately and then meta-analysed with two published lithium response GWAS datasets. Post-GWAS analyses were conducted to examine lithium response heritability and its genetic correlations with other traits. We also attempted to replicate past polygenic risk scores (PRS) results. RESULTS: SNP rs116927879 (A/G) was associated with lithium response at a genome-wide significance level (p = 4.509 × 10-08) with a consistent effect across all cohorts. rs116927879 is located on chromosome 7 and maps to the protein-coding gene ADCY1 and two pseudo-genes, GTF2IP13 and SEPT7P2.   • AB=depression

As rising rates of mental health problems among young people are reported across health systems worldwide,1 a contentious debate has emerged: do such rates indicate a bona fide increase in the need for mental health care or do these trends reflect an increasing medicalisation of ordinary distress? In The Lancet Psychiatry, Vicky Taxiarchi and colleagues2 contribute important evidence to advance understanding of this question by examining changes in characteristics, treatment patterns, and subsequent risks associated with first recorded anxiety or depression symptoms or diagnoses in a primary care population of more than 6 million adolescents in England between 2001 and 2023.

Depression affects approximately one in three people following a stroke, most commonly within the first year. The current standard of care for post-stroke depression (PSD) does not differ from that of a non-stroke patient. Few studies have investigated the application of osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT) within psychiatric conditions; however, studies have demonstrated its potential in downregulating the body's stress response. In this case report, we explore the use of OMT as an adjunct intervention for new-onset mild depressive symptoms following a stroke. This case follows a 64-year-old woman who presented to an outpatient behavioral health clinic in October 2024 for depressed mood following a left middle cerebral artery stroke four months prior. She initiated psychotherapy and declined medication management. After four months of psychotherapy exclusively, her mood symptoms continued to worsen and her PHQ-9 was 7. In April 2025, after six months of psychotherapy, she began OMT every two weeks, for a total of three treatments, addressing somatic dysfunctions of the head, cervical spine, thoracic inlet, and associated musculature. Self-Burdensomeness Scale: Validation and Measurement Invariance in Two German Samples.

Paper Archives of suicide research : official journal of the International Academy for Suicide Research pubmed 2026-11-21 doi:10.1080/13811118.2026.2764521
命中依据
  • AB=depression

OBJECTIVE: Perceiving oneself as a burden to oneself is related to suicidal ideation and behaviors. The Self-Burdensomeness Scale (SBS) is a promising instrument for assessing this construct. However, its factor structure, measurement invariance across demographic and clinical groups, and validity have not been comprehensively examined. METHOD: To address this, we examined (1) the latent factor structure of the SBS, (2) measurement invariance across gender, age groups, and between clinical and non-clinical samples, as well as (3) its construct and incremental validity. Data were drawn from a population-based sample (N = 4277) and a psychotherapy outpatient sample (N = 319). RESULTS: In both samples, the assumed one-factor model of the SBS was confirmed. The SBS showed measurement invariance across gender, age groups, and population type. Importantly, the SBS demonstrated incremental validity, by predicting suicidal ideation beyond the effects of depression and self-esteem. CONCLUSION: Overall, our findings indicate that the SBS is a valid measure of self-burdensomeness that can be used in non-clinical and clinical samples as well as in different age groups.

Overall, 382 (62.7%) of participants completed final assessments at the last planned study visit. Attrition was highest during the first year of life and declined thereafter. Inflammation, expressed as interleukin-6 (IL-6), and the trait rumination subtypes brooding and reflection are implicated in depression, yet their temporal relationship remains unclear. In a 3-wave study of 132 adolescents (age: M = 14.12 years, SD = 0.53; female: 35.9%; 64.1% male; 41.7% Black, 43.9% White), we tested competing longitudinal mediation models. Unexpectedly, findings did not support IL-6 as a mediator of the association between brooding and depressive symptoms. Instead, results were more consistent with a model in which IL-6 predicted subsequent brooding, which in turn predicted depressive symptoms. Further, a significant indirect association emerged between IL-6 and later depressive symptoms through greater brooding; the corresponding indirect effect through reflection was nonsignificant. Our findings suggest that inflammatory and cognitive processes, brooding in particular, may operate as interconnected processes associated with depressive symptoms.

Epilepsy and trigeminal neuralgia (TN) are treated traditionally as unrelated disorders, one defined by recurrent seizures, the other by paroxysmal facial pain. Yet both share a core pathophysiological feature: regional loss of neuronal excitability control, driven by gain-of-function in voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav1.3, Nav1.6, Nav1.7); failure of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic inhibition, disruption of the blood-brain and blood-nerve barriers with transforming growth factor-β-mediated neuroinflammation; and emergent network hypersynchrony. Pharmacologically, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, gabapentin and baclofen act across both conditions; neuromodulation with repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation reduces excitability in epileptic foci and trigeminocervical circuits alike. Equine trigeminal-mediated headshaking (TMHS) presents as a spontaneous large-animal phenotype that matches this framework; affected horses show infraorbital trigeminal activation thresholds below 5 mA without structural lesion, seasonal and exercise-dependent fluctuation in clinical signs and partial response to percutaneous electrical nerve stimulation and magnesium supplementation. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) on anxiety, depression, quality of life (QoL), fatigue, and stress in adult cancer patients. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to September 22, 2025, identified 22 experimental and quasi-experimental studies, mostly randomized controlled trials. Independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Random effects meta-analyses were conducted with Knapp-Hartung adjustments for outcomes with few studies. Heterogeneity, subgroup, and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed, and publication bias was assessed. ACT significantly reduced anxiety, depression, fatigue, and stress while improving QoL. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were consistent, but heterogeneity, particularly in QoL, warrants caution. Despite significant heterogeneity in QoL and possible publication bias, ACT showed a consistent benefit across outcomes. However, the magnitude of pooled effects should be interpreted with caution.

PURPOSE: This prospective longitudinal study analyzed the trajectories and correlates of psychological distress during the first year after hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT). Younger age was associated with higher anxiety, while older age was associated with higher wellbeing. CONCLUSION: Distinct distress trajectories emerged across the first year of HCT recovery. PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Neurogastrointestinal motility disorders and disorders of gut-brain interaction (DGBI) are difficult to treat, particularly with pharmacotherapy alone. This review examines percutaneous electrical nerve field stimulation (PENFS) as a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, addressing its potential mechanistic rationale, clinical evidence, patient selection, practical implementation, and future directions of research. RECENT FINDINGS: PENFS appears to act through several pathways: limbic modulation via the central nucleus of the amygdala, altered vagal afferent signaling at the nucleus tractus solitarius, and effects on an enteric nervous system that continues to mature through adolescence. Randomized sham-controlled trials and a multicenter registry show improvement in pain, nausea, and disability alongside a favorable safety profile. Auricular allodynia and impaired cardiac vagal efficiency are emerging as markers of treatment response. PENFS is a safe, effective, non-pharmacologic option across the DGBI spectrum. Formal dose- and duration-response work, adult trials, and long-term durability data remain the principal gaps, though work is ongoing.

This contribution traces that pattern along the axis of neurostimulation, from Fritsch and Hitzig's experiments and Penfield's intraoperative mapping to contemporary therapeutic neuromodulation, and argues that the shift from the discrete locus to the distributed network, made conceivable by functional neuroimaging and connectomics, found its causal and clinical proving ground in stimulation rather than in observation. Mood disorders furnish the exemplary case. As a transformative technology in neuroengineering, brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) establish a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices, independent of peripheral neuromuscular circuits by decoding neural activity and enabling bidirectional feedback. This capability fundamentally reshapes the paradigm of human-machine interaction. Based on the integration depth of neural interfaces, BCIs can be classified into invasive, semi-invasive, and non-invasive approaches, each supporting a range of applications from motor control to cognitive monitoring through multiple paradigms. Despite rapid technological advances, comprehensive reviews examining the clinical implementation of BCIs remain limited. Existing literature often focuses on BCI applications for specific disorders or introduces the recent technological innovations, yet lacks systematic synthesis and critical reflection on real-world clinical translation. Neuroscience routinely describes memories as stored neural symbols, yet durable memory and successful retrieval do not establish a separately accessible symbolic vehicle. I distinguish retention, the claim that a physical change persists and later influences behavior, from symbolic storage, the stronger computational claim that a description can be accessed independently of the operation it specifies. The criterion is functional and system-relative and does not rule out neural activity as access. It requires specifying, before testing, the candidate vehicle, its proposed use, the system boundary, and an endogenous route reaching the vehicle without using it. DNA meets the criterion: replication preserves nucleotide sequence without producing the encoded gene product. Evidence from synapses and circuits establishes persistent, functionally useful organization but has not shown this separation for any neural memory vehicle; in these states, identified reads are executions that modify what they read. Age-related hearing loss (ARHL) is a common chronic sensory disorder among the elderly. It causes communication difficulties and is closely associated with cognitive decline and depression. The degeneration of cochlear spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) and early damage to ribbon synapses are crucial processes in ARHL. Since synaptic dysfunction often occurs before hair cell loss and threshold elevations, it contributes to hidden hearing loss and adversely affects the efficacy of cochlear implantation. However, the mechanisms by which synaptic injury drives SGN aging are not yet fully understood. This review systematically overviews the degeneration of ribbon synapses and SGN in ARHL, including the molecular and functional heterogeneity of SGN subtypes, the spatial and temporal patterns of ribbon synapses, the pathological mechanisms and the cell death pathways of SGN damage during aging. This review also identifies future research directions and emphasizes early intervention targets in ARHL, aiming to provide a systematic theoretical framework for the early prevention and clinical management of ARHL.

Advances in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and artificial intelligence enable the identification of neural signatures-patterns of brain activity linked to thoughts, emotions, and mental states. Next-generation BCIs, including adaptive deep brain stimulation, promise personalized treatment for movement and psychiatric conditions. However, their effectiveness depends on whether neural signatures accurately reflect individuals' experiences and clinical states. Because neural signatures are abstract, they require meaningful correlations with behavior, symptoms, and clinical outcomes. Ethical challenges arise when brain data, behavioral observations, and patient self-reports conflict, raising questions about whose knowledge matters and how to determine clinical "ground truth." The stress-enhanced fear learning (SEFL) effect refers to the phenomenon whereby prior exposure to a severe stressor sensitizes fear learning, such that subsequently mild or ambiguous experiences that are usually insufficient to produce fear in unstressed individuals become capable of forming strong fear memories. As such, SEFL is argued to result from a non-associative state of fear sensitization produced by stress that resembles some of the characteristics of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Here, we were interested in testing whether the SEFL effect requires activity within the lateral periaqueductal gray (lPAG), a region we know is important for the development of associative fear memories. Specifically, we optogenetically inhibited activity within the lPAG during the stressor that drives the SEFL effect. We found that this did not impact on SEFL, demonstrating that the neural circuits involved in allowing stress to sensitize fear learning are dissociable from those involved in the development of associative fear memories. Participants completed the DSS-B along with measures of PTSD/CPTSD symptoms, trauma exposure, and coping strategies. Confirmatory factor analyses compared five models, and measurement invariance across sexual orientation and gender identity groups was tested using multi-group CFA. The DSS-B showed good internal consistency (α = .86) and a factorial structure consistent with the original scale. Configural, metric, and scalar invariance were supported across groups. DSS-B scores were strongly associated with PTSD/CPTSD symptoms, trauma exposure, and avoidance-focused coping, supporting convergent validity. In the outpatient rehabilitation clinic of Amsterdam University Medical Center (UMC), high-intensity interval training (HIIT) is part of routine rehabilitation due to its time efficiency, safety, tolerability and multiple health benefits. This pilot study therefore primarily aims to determine the feasibility, acceptability and safety of a structured HIIT programme targeting apathy in PwP following STN-DBS. Measuring neurotransmission in the human brain could advance our understanding of disorders, including depression. Although fast-scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) has provided valuable insights into neurotransmission in animal models, its application to human systems remains challenging. Here, we present an FSCV-based framework for real-time serotonin measurements in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived three-dimensional (3D) neuronal cultures. We demonstrate reproducible detection of spontaneous and evoked serotonin release from 3D serotonergic spheroids and show that serotonin dynamics differ between serotonin reuptake inhibitors. We investigate how a molecular stress mediator influences serotonin signaling and antidepressant effectiveness. Finally, we extend the platform to co-cultures containing microglia-like cells to examine serotonin dynamics under inflammatory conditions. We present a translational, label-free technology to measure serotonin dynamics in real-time in human stem cell-derived models. This method studies serotonin regulation, with potential applications to drug development and the mechanistic dissection of psychiatric disorders, such as depression.

命中依据
  • AB=neuromodulation

Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts the neurovascular unit (NVU), notably impairing the blood-spinal cord barrier (BSCB), which undergoes a biphasic transformation from acute hyperpermeability to chronic fibrotic sclerosis. This dynamic remodeling creates a heterogeneous barrier that hinders effective drug delivery and limits therapeutic success. Here we integrate pathological characterization with computational molecular dynamics to rationally engineer extracellular vesicles (EVs) capable of receptor-mediated transcytosis across the fibrotic BSCB. Coupled with computational fluid dynamics-optimized hydrogel scaffolds and neuromodulation techniques, this approach promotes NVU repair, restores synaptic homeostasis, and facilitates neural circuit rewiring. This integrated framework advances precision SCI interventions by overcoming the evolving BSCB, offering a novel paradigm for enhancing functional recovery after traumatic SCI and informing therapeutic strategies for central nervous system disorders characterized by barrier dysfunction.

A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control.

Paper Nature pubmed 2026-11-18 doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11251-7 Neuromodulation
命中依据
  • AB=neuromodulation

Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1-3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune-metabolic homeostasis4-9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation.

The Role of TRPC6 in the Pathogenesis of Depression and Its Potential as a Therapeutic Target.

Paper Current neuropharmacology pubmed 2026-11-16 doi:10.2174/011570159X529706261023063752
命中依据
  • TI=depression

Transient receptor potential canonical 6 (TRPC6) is widely expressed in most human tissues and participates in a variety of physiological processes. As a key non-selectivecalcium-permeable cation channel in the central nervous system, it is believed to regulate excitatory synapse formation. Recent studies have shown that abnormal expression and function of TRPC6 play a core regulatory role in the pathogenesis of depression. Chronic stress is a major inducer of depression and leads to significant downregulation of TRPC6 expression in the hippocampus of mice, accompanied by insufficient activation of the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-TRPC6 signaling pathway. This subsequently causes impaired hippocampal synaptic plasticity and induces obvious depressive-like behaviors. Nevertheless, the precise role of TRPC6 in depression remains to be fully clarified. Here we present the latest progress on the function and significance of TRPC6 in this disease. Downregulation of TRPC6 appears to be a key molecular mechanism in the pathogenesis of depression, and targeting TRPC6 expression may exert antidepressant effects by protecting hippocampal neurons and improving synaptic plasticity.

INTRODUCTION: Experimental studies and a previous small, randomized trial suggest that atomoxetine, a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, may be efficacious in the prevention or disease modification of Alzheimer's disease (AD). The primary outcome was AD, determined using a validated algorithm. We estimated 5- and 10-year risk ratios (RRs) and risk differences (RDs). Analyses were examined overall and by indication. RESULTS: This study included 70,367 person-trials (74.6% ≥70 years; 59.5% female; 86.7% non-Hispanic White). Initiation of atomoxetine versus no initiation was not associated with 5- or 10-year risk of AD but was associated with lower risk of AD-free death. In indication-specific analyses, atomoxetine was associated with lower 5-year risk of AD and AD-free death among individuals with depression. DISCUSSION: Initiation of atomoxetine was not associated with lower risk of AD later in life. The lower risk of AD among people with depression warrants further study.

Paper medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences pubmed 2026-11-15 doi:10.64898/2026.11.12.26367797
命中依据
  • AB=depression

Depression and anxiety are often assessed weeks or months apart with brief questionnaires covering few symptoms, leaving changes between assessments unobserved. Here, we introduce TALQ, a scoring system in which a large language model rates 52 symptoms from text, and use it to score 491 members of two online mental health communities every two weeks for a year. Ratings were stable across samples, predicted human annotations of interpersonal risk factors, low self-esteem and depression severity, and agreed with inventories completed by the same model. The scores mapped into 12 replicable symptom factors, including fearful preoccupation and social strain. Sleep disturbance and self-harm content consistently preceded overwhelm and emotional pain, respectively, two weeks later. People differed mainly in the states they occupied rather than transitions between them, and 13% entered in a crisis that remitted over months. Overall, our findings suggest that TALQ can measure expressed mental states densely and quantify longitudinal dynamics.

Metabolic psychiatry links severe mental illness to impaired brain and systemic energy metabolism, yet few treatments directly target this pathway. Metformin is widely prescribed to limit antipsychotic (AP)-induced weight gain, but growing evidence suggests it also influences central nervous system function. This narrative review organizes findings from cellular, animal, and human studies into a three-step model connecting cellular bioenergetics to brain network (BN) homeostasis. This proposed central cascade rests almost entirely on rodent and cellular studies, where metformin activates neuronal AMP-activated protein kinase, modulates gene regulation, and dampens microglial inflammation to support synaptic plasticity. In clinical trials, starting metformin alongside antipsychotics (APs) reliably reduces weight gain and insulin resistance (IR). A small number of preliminary clinical trials in schizophrenia and bipolar depression also report improved prefrontal-hippocampal connectivity or mood symptom relief, with psychiatric gains occurring mainly in patients whose peripheral IR resolves. Bergmann glia: The silent architect shaping cerebellar cortex.

Paper Tissue & cell pubmed 2026-11-15 doi:10.1016/j.tice.2026.104134
命中依据
  • AB=depression

The cerebellum is a brain structure that regulates motor functions and cognitive processes. Recent molecular and embryological studies have clarified its cellular development and the intercellular interactions that guide it. These studies have provided a framework for exploring molecular mechanisms underlying pattern formation, neurogenesis, fate determination, and prenatal and postnatal cell migration. This article focuses on the development, structure, identifying markers, and function of Bergmann glial cells (BGCs), which are crucial for the folding of the cerebellar surface, the proper functioning of the cerebellar neuronal circuit, and nervous pathology. BGCs offer a promising therapeutic target for central nervous system (CNS) disorders, with impaired cells being linked to abnormalities seen in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), long-term synaptic depression (LTD), and vanishing white matter (VWM). In conclusion, the evidence positions BGCs as active organizers of cerebellar circuitry and as candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets whose disease-specific roles require further mechanistic validation.

Exposure and response prevention (ERP) is a gold-standard treatment for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and there is increasing interest in intensive approaches that provide treatment over a shortened timeframe. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is an FDA-approved treatment for OCD that has similarly attracted interest in accelerated protocols. Yet there have been no reports on the combined use of intensive ERP ('iERP') and accelerated TMS ('aTMS'). Here, we demonstrate the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating iERP and aTMS. We provided a 5-day course of aTMS-iERP for refractory OCD, with each day consisting of 8 ERP sessions in between 10 TMS sessions. In patients with severe and refractory OCD this novel approach was well tolerated, with positive clinical effects observed in each patient (N = 5). These early feasibility data suggest that innovative approaches to brain stimulation and psychotherapy should be explored not just in isolation but in combination with each other.

E2 decline was associated with FasL loss, increased IL-7 and IL-15, altered dendritic-cell phenotype, and activation of TNFα- and IL-17A-producing TM, which strongly correlated with Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale scores. Paper Research square pubmed 2026-11-10 doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-11407094/v1 Major depressive disorder
命中依据

Many patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) do not respond to their first antidepressant, and clinicians lack an empirical basis for deciding whether to continue or change treatment after an initial trial. We analysed the Precision Medicine in Mental Health Care (PRIME) pragmatic randomized controlled trial, in which 1,944 US veterans were randomized to usual care enhanced by pharmacogenetic testing or to usual care alone. Using decision tree analysis in the 1,307 participants who had not responded after four weeks, four characteristics separated those with the highest (39.9±10.5%) and the lowest (11.1±3.0%) likelihood of week-12 treatment response: symptom improvement at week 4, better physical health, availability of pharmacogenetic test results, and absence of post-traumatic stress disorder. The resulting decision-support tool identified 77% of week-4 partial and non-responders as candidates for a treatment change. This preliminary tool requires validation in independent samples before prospective clinical evaluation.

命中依据

The corticospinal tract (CST) is a neural pathway that supports skilled use of the arm and hand. Lesions of corticospinal axons result in muscle weakness, deficits of gross motor function, and loss of proximal and distal dexterous control for which effective treatments are still lacking. Here we exploited excitatory connections from motor thalamus to primary motor cortex to potentiate surviving descending signals and restore volitional arm and hand control in three monkeys with corticospinal tract lesion, using deep brain stimulation. Stimulation targeted to thalamocortical projections facilitated upper-limb movements, enabling monkeys with arm and hand paralysis to perform unconstrained 3D reach and fine dexterous tasks. Stimulation improved strength, hand gross motor function, and digits control. Electrophysiology suggested that effects were mediated by and more effective when targeting fibers with monosynaptic connection to the corticospinal motoneurons. Stimulation was delivered in continuous with FDA-clinically approved parameters holding realistic promises of clinical translation.

Psychiatric states manifest over multiple timescales, from transient fluctuations in disorder-related distress to long-term variations in disease severity, yet whether these expressions share common neural representations remains unknown. We analyzed intracranial recordings from the ventral capsule and orbitofrontal cortex spanning more than 4595 patient-days in 8 individuals undergoing deep brain stimulation therapy, together with quantitative facial- and speech-derived behavioral measures. The biological mechanisms governing recovery versus chronicity of adverse posttraumatic neuropsychiatric sequelae (APNS) remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized longitudinal molecular changes among trauma survivors across ten APNS domains, including pain, anxiety, and depression. Recovery across these diverse clinical outcomes was associated with a shared, temporally coordinated transcriptional signature, characterized by early innate immune activation, subsequent homeostatic and wound-healing processes, and later adaptive immune responses. In contrast, chronic APNS trajectories exhibited limited transcriptional remodeling. Evidence from psychology, neuroscience, microbiology, and nutritional psychiatry is integrated to evaluate the roles of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activation, reward processing, neurotransmitter metabolism, immune signaling, appetite-related hormones, and microbial metabolites. We report on a 21-year-old woman with N2O dependence who, after 6 months of repeated N2O inhalation, developed gait instability, limb numbness and tremors, accompanied by delusions and auditory hallucinations. During her first hospitalization, she was treated with antipsychotics and vitamin B12; however, she relapsed to N2O use shortly after discharge and was readmitted. Upon her second admission, she received 10 sessions of 10 Hz repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. Her craving for N2O began to decline after the third session and continued to improve after the sixth, with dependence largely resolved by the end of the treatment course. No adverse events, such as headache or tinnitus, and no significant withdrawal symptoms were observed during treatment. The patient was followed up 3 times after discharge and had maintained abstinence from N2O for 3 months (12 weeks) since her last use, remaining emotionally stable and resuming normal daily life and work. 命中依据

Precise modulation of brain networks for tongue motor and sensory control (TMSC) is critical for neruorehabilitation. Existing neuromodulation approaches use fixed targets, ignoring individual network architecture. We present an AI-driven, individualized fMRI neuromodulation (iNM) platform adaptively targeting subject-specific TMSC networks in real-time. Using a neurofunctional twin built from each participant's anatomy and function, iNM reinforces targeted activity and suppresses competing states. Unsupervised machine learning and hidden Markov modeling showed iNM increased TMSC-state occupancy from 82% to 97% and suppressed swallow-state interference by 83%. The inferior parietal lobule emerged as a sensorimotor integration hub, with increased magnitude (d' 90.4 right, 84 left) and spatial expansion (134.8% right, 81.8% left). Cortico-subcortical connectivity strengthened 53% to 74% across motor, sensory, and attention networks and persisted into non-iNM blocks. Thus, iNM may offer precision neurorehabilitation for CNS or PNS disorders, such as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, and treatment-induced cranial neuropathy in head-and-neck-cancer survivors, respectively.

Tectonic movements and related depositional responses are always complicated in a typical foreland basin. This study investigates the provenance and depositional facies of the Cretaceous Yageliemu Formation in the Kuqa Depression, Tarim Basin, NW China, to determine favorable reservoir distribution. Evidence from detrital zircon U-Pb age and heavy mineral assemblages illustrates two mainly provenances: (1) the Kelasu River characterized by the U-Pb age from 220 to 400 Ma and 420 to 560 Ma and the heavy mineral assemblages of leucoxene, zircon, and barite; (2) the Kuqa River dominated by the U-Pb age from 300 to 520 Ma and the heavy mineral assemblages of barite and apatite. Integration of core, well logging curves, and seismic responses indicates that the Yageliemu Formation can be subdivided into three parasequence sets: EL2, EL1, and LL1. The parasequence sets of EL2 and EL1 are favorable for the development and accumulation of large-scale sand bodies. The sediments in the Yageliemu Formation mainly consist of pebbly sandstone, coarse- to fine-grained sandstone, siltstone, and silty mudstone deposited in a braided-river delta front setting. Acid-sensing ion channels in pain and psychiatric disorders: from basic properties to comorbidity mechanisms.

Paper Frontiers in pharmacology pubmed 2026-11-03 doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1967840
命中依据
  • AB=depression

Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that mediate Na+ and Ca2+ influx upon activation by extracellular acidification. Beyond protons, endogenous ligands, toxins, and small molecules modulate ASIC gating through direct or synergistic mechanisms. ASICs have emerged as key players in pain and psychiatric disorders. Tissue acidosis drives hyperalgesia via sustained ASIC activation, synaptic plasticity disruption, and central sensitization, thereby promoting chronic pain. In limbic circuits, ASIC1a expression in the amygdala, periaqueductal gray, and dorsal raphe nucleus links these channels to anxiety and depression, with ASIC1a antagonists demonstrating robust efficacy in preclinical models. Selective ASIC modulators represent promising therapeutic candidates for pain-psychiatric comorbidities. This review integrates ASIC biophysical properties with their molecular and circuit-level mechanisms in disease, offering a framework to guide future translational efforts targeting ASIC-mediated pathologies.

[New surgical therapies for essential tremor].

Paper Nederlands tijdschrift voor geneeskunde pubmed 2026-11-03 Deep brain stimulationBrain stimulation
命中依据
  • AB="deep brain stimulation"

Essential tremor is a common and often progressive movement disorder that can lead to significant functional impairment, social isolation, and care dependency. Despite available treatments, patients are frequently referred late for advanced therapy. This article illustrates management options through two cases of patients with longstanding, medication-refractory tremor. Both experienced substantial disabilities affecting daily activities and quality of life. Patient A underwent deep brain stimulation (DBS), resulting in marked tremor reduction. Patient B underwent an MRI-guided focused ultrasound thalamotomy, achieving immediate and lasting unilateral tremor control without implantation of a device. Pharmacological therapy remains first-line but is often insufficient or limited by side effects. After failure of two adequately trialed medications, timely referral to a neurosurgical center is recommended. DBS and HIFU are effective, evidence-based treatments, each with distinct advantages and limitations. Earlier consideration of these interventions can significantly improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

However, outcomes for conditions outside PTSD are often mixed, particularly for craving, relapse, and repetitive behavioral endpoints. Existing clinical models can be helpful but lack specific guidance on EMDR procedures in such cases. Extending previous predictive processing (PP) accounts of EMDR that have focused primarily on PTSD and traumatic memory, we propose a transdiagnostic framework informed by PP theory. Therein, psychopathology is the result of the persistence of overly precise, maladaptive predictions that guide perception, bodily experience, emotion, and action, despite contradictory sensory input. We hypothesize that PTSD, SUDs, and BFRBs differ in the focal content, hierarchical level, temporal scope, and automaticity (proceduralization) of dominant predictions. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder closely linked to metabolic dysfunction, including obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. These comorbidities are associated with poorer treatment response, yet pharmacological options for PTSD remain limited. Here, we review evidence that PTSD and metabolic disease share convergent mechanisms, including dysregulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, glucocorticoid receptor signaling, neuroinflammation, insulin resistance and mitochondrial dysfunction. We evaluate the rationale for repurposing approved cardiometabolic drugs, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, insulin sensitizers, statins, renin-angiotensin system modulators and glial-targeting agents. We critically assess preclinical and clinical evidence, highlight current limitations and propose a biomarker-guided framework to match therapies to dominant biological mechanisms. Finally, we discuss the exceptional burden of PTSD with cardiometabolic disease in war-affected Ukraine as a priority setting for future mechanism-based clinical trials. Health care professionals face many challenges in practice for which collegial and peer support can be impactful. Some of the most seemingly insurmountable struggles result from medical error or an adverse patient outcome. Clinicians may experience remorse, guilt, sadness, burnout, depression, and isolation, potentially causing second victim syndrome. In addition, medical professionals face daily frustrations due to loss of clinical autonomy, operational pressures, shrinking margins, workforce shortages, misaligned institutional incentives, and corporatization of health systems that can lead to burnout and moral injury. It is therefore critically important to support clinicians and ensure that those who dedicate their lives to caring for others feel heard, have a safe and supportive sounding board to debrief stressful situations, and do not feel abandoned. Collegial networks and peer support are important and helpful resources. This article reviews key aspects of collegial and peer support programs that can benefit health care professionals in allergy-immunology and beyond.

Sleep disorders can perpetuate mental health conditions and negative social interactions. Additionally, research shows that individuals who develop socially debilitating disorders like PTSD, anxiety, and depression also report increased sleep disturbances. Exacerbating this issue, increased sleep debt due to sleep disruption from mental illness can potentiate further sleep dysregulation. Chronic social stress can lead to the development of sleep disorders, due to negative interactions in both natural and manmade power dynamics (including parent, employer, and even government related stressors). Hierarchical dynamics can lead to inequitable treatment and widespread health consequences, due to environmentally-imposed social dominance. Paper ACS pharmacology & translational science pubmed 2026-10-09 doi:10.1021/acsptsci.6c00463
命中依据
  • AB=depression

Imprinted genes, expressed from only one parental allele, contribute to neurodevelopmental and mood disordersincluding depression, bipolar disorder, and anxietythrough mechanisms such as dosage imbalance, early adversity, sex-specific epigenetic changes, and altered imprinting in the placenta or blood. Key imprinted genes including paternal IGF2 and DLK1, maternal H19, MEG3 and UBE3A, and complex GRB10 regulate neurogenesis, neuronal differentiation, and synaptic plasticity, suggesting that restoring imprint balance may serve as a therapeutic target. This review provides a comprehensive summary of the molecular mechanisms, regulatory characteristics, and methodologies associated with imprinted genes, emphasizing their parent-specific epigenetic roles in neural circuits and development. We also summarize their roles in neuropsychiatric and affective disorders. A deeper understanding of the complex interplay between imprinted genes and their regulatory networks is essential for developing targeted interventions for neural development and emotional neurological disorders.

Sleep disorders are prevalent among psychiatric patients and are strongly associated with neurobiological, psychological, and behavioral processes. This chapter analyzes neuroscience-informed psychoeducation (NIPE), an approach incorporating the insights gained from neuroscience with patient education to understand and manage sleep disturbances better. To establish a scientific basis for psychoeducational interventions, we discuss central mechanisms of sleep regulation such as circadian rhythms, sleep homeostasis, neurotransmitter systems, and brain networks. It illustrates how bidirectional sleep disorders and psychiatric syndromes, including depression, anxiety, PTSD, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), are linked, and explains sleep disturbance as a transdiagnostic key clinical feature. In addition to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, NIPE is used to provide a solution to insomnia by integrating mindfulness-based strategies and personalized interventions with the assistance of digital technologies. Cardiac and psychological diseases refer to a clinical syndrome with or without organic cardiovascular disease, characterized by cardiovascular somatic symptoms associated with adverse emotions. Modern medicine mainly adopts a regimen of foundational cardiovascular therapy combined with anti-anxiety and antidepressant drugs for this condition. While this approach can partially alleviate symptoms, clinical challenges persist, including frequent gastrointestinal adverse reactions, the potential for dependence on psychotropic drugs, and poor long-term medication adherence among patients. TCM, adhering to the principle of simultaneous cardiac and psychological treatment and simultaneous regulation of the body and spirit, holds unique advantages in managing this condition. However, the current clinical understanding of the TCM pathogenesis of cardiac and psychological diseases remains fragmented, and the treatment strategies using classic TCM formulas lack systematic organization and integration. BACKGROUND: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) has emerged as a major global public health challenge. Recently, Stanford neuromodulation therapy, a paradigm of individualized target-transcranial magnetic stimulation (IT-TMS) focusing on the subgenual anterior cingulate cortex (sgACC), has exhibited significant therapeutic benefits in treating MDD. The pregenual anterior cingulate cortex (pgACC), alongside the sgACC, is also an emotional subregion of the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). This study aims to explore the safety and efficacy of IT-TMS targeting the pgACC for the treatment of MDD. METHODS: This is a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial involving 68 patients with MDD randomly assigned to an IT-TMS group and a sham group. The IT-TMS group receives individualized intermittent theta-burst stimulation targeted at the region in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) with the strongest negative functional connectivity to the pgACC. The sham group undergoes a well-accepted 90°-reversed sham stimulation procedure. The primary outcome is the percentage change in the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAMD-17) score from baseline to the end of treatment.

With the emergence of the gut-brain axis, inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is no longer simply regarded as a localized intestinal disease but as a systemic disorder intimately associated with psychiatric comorbidities, including anxiety and depression. However, conventional therapeutic strategies predominantly target localized colonic inflammation, which often yields suboptimal outcomes. This highlights a critical need for gut-brain co-therapy to achieve comprehensive IBD management. Based on our observation that indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) possesses the potential to attenuate hippocampal neuroinflammation and subsequently modulate intestinal inflammation via the acetylcholine pathway, we engineered a gut-brain co-therapy delivery platform (CB-ASA/IAA/L). This system comprises Clostridium butyricum (CB) loaded with 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA), encapsulated by a pH-responsive Eudragit L100-55 layer incorporating IAA. This microecological preparation is based on effective protection and delivery of CB, achieving the delivery of IAA to the brain and 5-ASA to the colon simultaneously. Deimos's shape and geology explained by a subcatastrophic impact.

Paper Nature astronomy pubmed 2026-08-18 doi:10.1038/s41550-026-02956-w
命中依据
  • AB=depression

Small planetary bodies record the processes that shaped the Solar System, but their surfaces and interiors often evolve in unexpected ways. Deimos, the potato-shaped, 12-km-diameter outer satellite of Mars, has a strikingly smooth surface covered by fine regolith, in contrast to its heavily cratered and grooved sibling, 22-km-diameter Phobos. Moreover, Deimos's topography is dominated by a single large south-polar depression, whose formation we simulate to constrain the moon's interior and surface geomechanical properties and to explain the origin and distribution of its regolith. Here we find that an oblique impact by a 320-m-diameter projectile can quantitatively account for this depression, the global regolith layer and surface features such as bright streaks and crater infill. Our results show that Deimos's upper layers are extremely weak and that its interior is highly porous and dissipative, resembling the recently visited rubble-pile asteroids rather than lunar regolith. This suggests that small dark moons and asteroids, despite their specific histories, may converge on similar physical states.

Paper Handbook of clinical neurology pubmed 2026 doi:10.1016/B978-0-443-27442-8.00009-3 Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
命中依据
  • TI="transcranial magnetic stimulation"

Transcranial magnetic stimulation cannot only excite but also inhibit the human brain, giving rise to negative motor phenomena such as the contralateral and ipsilateral silent periods (CoSP, ISP). These terms refer to the transient suppression of voluntary electromyographic activity following the application of magnetic stimuli in the contra- or ipsilateral motor cortex, respectively. This chapter presents in detail the current understanding of the cortical and subcortical mechanisms underlying the generation of these silent periods and summarizes their physiologic role in motor control. CoSP and ISP are deceptively easy to elicit. In fact, careful parametrization is required in order to register and analyze these phenomena in an optimal manner. Finally, there is a multitude of endogenous and exogenous factors that modify and shape CoSP and ISP, and these are critically presented and discussed. It is argued that the investigation of silent periods advances our knowledge of inhibitory brain mechanisms and provides a window to gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-related function and dysfunction in health and disease.

Electroencephalography (EEG) in combination with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) opens up the possibility to measure brain responses to TMS. This is a relatively novel technology that significantly extends the longer-established technologies of TMS of the motor cortex (M1) and recording of motor evoked responses via electromyography. TMS-EEG of M1 results in a typical sequence of TMS-evoked responses (TEPs), such as the P30, N45, P60, N100, and P200. TEPs constitute spatiotemporally complex waveforms that arise from both local neuronal activation and recurrent neuronal activity propagated across multiple cortical and subcortical regions. Response components<70 ms are caused by direct TMS effects, while later responses are significantly contaminated by peripherally evoked potentials caused by the auditory and somatosensory inputs from the TMS pulse. P30 reflects local M1 excitability controlled by voltage-gated ion channels, while N45 and P60 reflect excitation-inhibition balance controlled by GABAAergic and glutamatergic neurotransmission. This chapter reviews magnetic brain stimulation techniques designed to induce neural plasticity in the motor cortex. Originally developed as repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with a fixed rate, several protocols have since emerged to produce longer-lasting effects more efficiently, such as theta-burst stimulation, paired associative stimulation, repetitive paired-pulse TMS, and quadripulse stimulation. Additionally, transcranial static magnetic stimulation applies static magnetic fields to the brain. These techniques have advanced our ability to modulate cortical excitability and promote neuroplasticity, particularly influencing excitatory and inhibitory circuits in the motor cortex in a manner mimicking long-term potentiation and long-term depression. This would help us better understand how cortical circuits can be reprogrammed. Clinically, these methods leverage the brain's adaptability and hold therapeutic potential for neurologic and psychiatric disorders, including stroke rehabilitation, depression, neurodegenerative diseases, and enhancing motor learning and cognitive function. INTRODUCTION: Obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) affects about 1-2% of the global population, with roughly 30% of patients not responding to first-line treatments. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has some support for treatment-resistant OCD but global use is unclear. METHODS: This study describes the frequency with which TMS was reported to be received among a large cohort of individuals who self-identified as Latino-Hispanic in Latin America and the United States. Among 3391 participants, 76 (2.2%) had completed TMS for OCD. RESULTS: Recipients who received TMS exhibited more severe current and lifetime OCD symptoms compared to non-recipients. On average, participants underwent 22.61 TMS sessions (SD=20.96), and self-reported experiencing minimal to some improvement from TMS. The majority of TMS recipients were from Brazil (n=26), Mexico (n=17) and USA (n=16). CONCLUSIONS: Findings suggest that TMS does not appear to be widely used in OCD treatment among the Latino-Hispanic population, particularly in Latin American countries. Further study of TMS efficacy and dissemination in underserved regions is warranted.

命中依据

Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a noninvasive technique used to probe and modulate brain activity that has significantly enhanced our understanding of voluntary motor control. By disrupting or enhancing neural function with temporally precise ("online") or sustained ("offline") stimulation protocols, TMS has revealed how primary motor, premotor, and posterior parietal cortices contribute to motor execution, reaction time, action selection, reach planning, and grasp kinematics. Single-pulse and repetitive TMS protocols enable precise mapping of both the timing and the functional role of a brain region's involvement in voluntary movement. Dual-coil TMS protocols further allow for the measurement and modulation of trans-cortical connectivity, clarifying how distributed brain areas coordinate complex actions. These various TMS approaches have also helped elucidate mechanisms of motor learning, cortical plasticity, and use-dependent adaptation. TMS is a useful tool for establishing causal links between neural circuits and voluntary motor control and holds therapeutic potential for motor rehabilitation.

Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial electric stimulation (TES), by providing a noninvasive access to cortical circuits, improved the knowledge on the pathophysiology of the motor system and opened the way to neuromodulatory interventions. To capture the physiologic basis of these brain stimulation methods, spinal epidural recordings have been used to obtain a direct measure of the corticospinal activity evoked by TES and TMS, both in animals and in humans. Here, we review the experimental evidence that has provided insight into the site of activation at a cortical circuit level by different stimulation protocols. This knowledge also led to the construction of neural network models explaining and testing the effects of stimulation on the output recorded from corticospinal axons. Over more than 20 years, models of two broad categories have been constructed: single-corticospinal cell-based models and more complex neuronal network-based models. Mixed models have also been proposed.

Ultrasound-based neuromodulation includes magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound and low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation. Both utilize acoustic energy to reach deep brain structures with high spatial precision through the intact skull. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound produces precise thermal ablation, whereas transcranial ultrasound stimulation uses low-intensity, pulsed sonication to reversibly modulate neuronal excitability without tissue damage. This chapter reviews their methodological principles, mechanisms of action, and clinical applications of ultrasound in motor system disorders. Magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound is an approved incisionless alternative to surgical lesion or deep brain stimulation for treatment of essential tremor and Parkinson disease, with accurate lesioning of thalamic and pallidal targets under MRI guidance. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable direct interaction between neural activity and external devices or neuromodulatory systems, offering novel approaches for restoring, rehabilitating, and modulating motor function following neurologic injury and disease. Over recent decades, BCIs have progressed from experimental demonstrations of operant conditioning to clinically relevant technologies applied in stroke, spinal cord injury, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, movement disorders, and other motor syndromes. This chapter presents a critical, clinically focused review of motor BCIs, with emphasis on clinical applications rather than technical fundamentals. Key topics include invasive and noninvasive signal acquisition methods, anatomic targets for recording and stimulation, decoding and artificial intelligence approaches, and actuator systems such as robotics, functional electrical stimulation, and spinal or cortical neuromodulation. Some theoretical concepts support the use of certain "excitability-decreasing" NIBS protocols (rTMS delivered at low frequency or as continuous θ burst stimulation (cTBS), or cathodal tDCS) applied to motor cortical regions to alleviate dystonia. PURPOSE: This study assessed the prevalence and correlates of depressive symptoms among travestis and transgender women in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the Transcendendo cohort (2015-2023) using baseline data from travestis and transgender women aged ≥18. Sociodemographics, HIV status, at-risk substance use, violence victimization, and sexual partnership characteristics were analyzed as correlates in a modified Poisson regression model with a log link and robust variance to obtain adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs). Development and validation of a 3-item Transportation Security Index for social risk screening assessments and research into the many pathways through which transportation impacts health.

Paper AJE advances : research in epidemiology pubmed 2025-11-17 doi:10.1093/ajeadv/uuaf020 Major Depression
命中依据
  • AB=depression

Clinicians and researchers studying transportation as a social determinant of health need measurement tools that screen for people with transportation problems and reveal the pathways through which transportation impacts health. Existing versions of the Transportation Security Index (TSI), a validated measure of transportation insecurity, are lengthy, making their use in research and clinical settings difficult. In this paper, we identify and validate an abbreviated 3-item TSI. We derive the TSI-3 from its 6-item counterpart (TSI-6) by analyzing 2022 survey data representative of the US population aged 25 years and older and content expert feedback. To validate the TSI-3, we embedded a split-ballot experiment in a 2024 survey with a similar sampling frame. We compared the TSI-3 and TSI-6's psychometric properties, ability to distinguish between transportation secure and insecure people, prevalence estimates, and associations with self-rated health and major depression. Results demonstrate that the TSI-3 is an effective substitute for the TSI-6 and is faster to administer by 56%. However, whereas the TSI-6 identifies 3 categories of transportation insecurity, the TSI-3 identifies 2.

Transitional psychiatry addresses the complex process through which individuals move from adolescence to adulthood, both in terms of developmental stage and mental healthcare systems. This transition includes the shift from pediatric to adult psychiatric services, as well as the evolution from vague or subclinical symptoms to established psychiatric disorders that may become chronic without early intervention. Psychiatric disorders often emerge early in life: approximately 50% before age 15 and 75% before age 25. Early detection and intervention are therefore crucial to improving long-term mental health outcomes, functional independence, and social integration. However, current healthcare systems frequently fail to meet the needs of adolescents and young adults during this critical transition phase. Organizational discontinuities and clinical complexity lead to several risks: * Difficulties in accessing appropriate psychiatric care for adolescents presenting with emerging symptoms, * High rates of service disengagement for patients already receiving pediatric mental health care who do not successfully transition to adult services. Despite the efficacy of current evidence-based pharmacotherapies and psychotherapies for smoking cessation, alternative treatments are critically needed. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a non-invasive form of brain stimulation, US FDA-approved for smoking cessation. In this protocol, the investigators propose comparing the two rTMS protocols (standard TMS vs. precision TMS) to find a better treatment parameter for smoking cessation in Veterans. Identifying an efficacious rTMS protocol would benefit Veterans who want to quit smoking.

OvariAn Secretome and Integrated HealthSpan

The OASIS study aims to identify and characterize circulating molecular signatures associated with ovarian aging, and to determine how these signatures relate to multidomain healthspan during the menopausal transition. Part 2 is a prospective cohort of 300 women aged 40-50 years who will undergo comprehensive clinical, gynecological, and molecular assessments over 24 months, followed by individualized medical management based on their clinical findings. Part 3 (PRISM) is a nested substudy involving up to 30 women from the prospective cohort who will undergo intensive hormonal and ultrasound monitoring across a single menstrual cycle.

NQ TMS for MDD Therapy Using 1 Day x 3 Sessions Protocol for Adult Patient

Clinical Trial trials 2026-11-20 Transcranial Magnetic StimulationMajor depressive disorder

Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) Therapy is a non-invasive procedure that uses magnetic pulses to stimulate the cortex (brain) to treat Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). Currently established therapy uses one 19-minute treatment session per day for 5 days per week for 6 weeks, for a total of 30 treatment sessions. The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of an accelerated but shortened TMS dosing regimen for adults with MDD aged 22-85. Participants in this study will be subjected to the same 19-minutes treatment session, but three times on the same day, and only for one day. This will greatly reduce the logistical burden of completing the therapy regime.

The overall purpose of this study is to better understand human cognition and human epilepsy by working with patients undergoing clinical treatment for pharmacologically resistant epilepsy. The investigators will investigate human cognition by conducting controlled experiments that focus on sensory, motor, and cognitive phenomena such as sensory processing, memory, and language. The investigators will also examine the neural underpinnings of epilepsy during both sleep and wakefulness to better understand both the foundations of epilepsy and how epilepsy affects cognition. The investigators hope to use these data to have a better understanding of cognition, epilepsy, and how the two interact. Music Listening for Mental Health Recovery After Stroke

Clinical Trial trials 2026-11-20 Cognition

This study aims to explore whether listening to music intentionally can support the mental health of people recovering from a stroke. The question the investigators aim to answer is: Can intentional music listening improve emotional well-being in stroke survivors? And if so, what kinds of changes might music listening induce in mental health, thinking and memory (cognition), and brain activity? Participants will be randomly assigned to listen to either music or an audiobook for one hour each day, at home, for four weeks. Participants will also attend four in-person sessions with the researchers: at the start of the study (baseline), just before the listening period begins, after the four weeks are complete, and at a follow-up. During these visits, researchers will gather information about participants' mood and mental health (via questionnaires), assess memory and attention (via cognitive tasks), and use MRI scans to look at brain activity.

Participants will be randomized into either the control group (educational information) or the intervention group (educational information; personalized physical activity plan; activity tracker watch; access to a private, online survivor community; motivational text messages and check-in calls/e-mails). Clinical Trial trials 2026-11-20

This is a concurrent exploratory mixed methods study that involves the use of a quantitative and a qualitative approach. For the quantitative study, aims are to describe any possible relation between the identified factors with HRQoL and participation in individuals with MM and with reactions to caring and self-efficacy of caregivers. Effect of Peripartum 40 Hz Audiovisual Stimulation on Postpartum Depression in Women Undergoing Elective Cesarean Section: A Randomized Clinical Trial

Clinical Trial trials 2026-11-20

Postpartum depression (PPD) is a common mental health condition affecting 10%-30% of new mothers, with serious consequences for both mother and child. Effective prevention is limited by barriers to psychological or pharmacological treatments. This study evaluates whether short-term 40 Hz light and sound stimulation during and immediately after elective cesarean section can reduce PPD risk. The intervention group receives three 30-minute sessions of combined 40 Hz flashing light and pulsed sound (starting after baby delivery, then at 24 and 48 hours postpartum). The control group receives identical non-flickering light and white noise as placebo.The main outcome is the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale score at 42 days postpartum. Secondary outcomes include depression rates, insomnia severity, and anxiety levels.Participants are women aged ≥18 years with single full-term pregnancy scheduled for elective cesarean section. Exclusion criteria include psychiatric disorders, epilepsy, or eye conditions affecting light sensitivity. If effective, this non-invasive, drug-free intervention could provide a safe and accessible PPD prevention strategy during routine cesarean delivery.

Effect of Clinical Pharmacist-Led Pharmaceutical Care in Major Depressive Disorder

Clinical Trial trials 2026-11-20 Major depressive disorder

This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of a six-month clinical pharmacist-led pharmaceutical care intervention on medication adherence, beliefs about medicines, and health-related quality of life in adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder (MDD) receiving antidepressant treatment. A total of 186 participants were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either structured pharmaceutical care in addition to usual psychiatric care or usual psychiatric care alone. Of these, 170 participants completed the six-month follow-up. The intervention included individualized patient counseling, medication review, identification and management of medication-related problems, and telephone follow-up every two weeks. Medication adherence was assessed using the Medication Adherence Report Scale (MARS-5), beliefs about medicines using the Turkish Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire (BMQ-T), and health-related quality of life using the EQ-5D-3L and EQ-VAS. Assessments were conducted at baseline, Month 3, and Month 6.

Providing care to individuals with serious mental illness can be challenging, requiring ongoing monitoring, treatment adjustments, and coordination of various medical and social services. Stressors and poor adherence with treatment are common and can lead to rapid worsening in symptoms, job loss, homelessness, incarceration, or suicide. Clinician visits can be infrequent. Patient-clinician contact between visits is challenging and often nonexistent. As such, illness exacerbations usually occur with no clinician awareness in real time, leaving limited opportunity to provide services. Clinicians need interventions that are capable of monitoring and quickly detecting worsening behaviors and illness, to improve care coordination, outreach, and treatment. This project studies the effectiveness of enhanced care coordination using passive mobile data monitoring and support from peer specialists, with the goal of improving outcomes and reducing the need for acute care.

Incontinence after prostate treatment (IPT) affects up to 25% of men following radical prostatectomy or other prostate therapies, primarily resulting from sphincteric weakness and impaired neuromuscular control. This proof-of-concept, prospective, randomized clinical trial aims to evaluate the safety, tolerability, acceptability, and procedural feasibility of targeting the pSMA using non-invasive repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in adult males with IPT, alongside a cohort of continent controls. A total of 23 participants will be enrolled (targeting 10 evaluable IPT subjects and 10 continent controls). Dialysis is important in treating people with end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) to remove excess water and toxins, maintaining quality of life (QoL) and to keep people alive. Where people with ESKD retain too much water (fluid overload), the amount of water removed and the speed of removal must be higher to meet the individual's needs and avoid short- and long-term negative consequences. This can be a particular issue for people on haemodialysis after a weekend, when there is a 2-day gap between dialysis sessions. Removing the larger quantities of water quickly (proportional to speed of removal) can lead to low blood pressure, reducing QoL and increasing the chance of getting heart and blood vessel disease and the risk of death. Additionally, the dialysis schedules, and lack of dialysis capacity, often means sessions cannot be extended, or patients are offered extra sessions for fluid removal. Given the need to reduce fluid overload and the difficulties people have sticking to fluid restrictions, (taken by mouth) other therapies are needed to improve outcomes and people's experiences.
